transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having a hard time getting past how my face and hands look. They seem rough and worn to me—cracks, spots, sagging. When I’m around bankers or county people, I feel like they’re staring at all of it. My wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, but… I can’t quite let it go.
Are you worried about how any other parts of your body look, or is it mainly your face and hands that bother you?

Mostly my face and hands. I mean… that’s what I get stuck on. The cracks and spots, the sagging, how worn they look. Especially if I’m around bankers or county folks, I feel like they’re noticing it. My wife says it’s just from working outside, but it still bothers me.
Do you think your face and hands actually look rough and worn, or is it just that you feel like they do?

I think they actually do look that way… rough, worn. The cracks and spots, the sagging. Maybe my wife’s right that it’s just from working outside, but when I’m around bankers or county people, it feels like it’s plain as day and they’re looking at it.
Is your concern about your face and hands interfering with your daily life or activities in any way?

Yeah… some. I’ve missed calls with bankers, put off decisions for the farm, just because I couldn’t get myself to look… presentable enough to sit down with people. And I don’t really agree to photos anymore, even when they’d help with the retreat or craft sales.
Do you think other people actually notice the cracks, spots, and sagging on your face and hands, or is it just a feeling you have?

I… I think they do notice. Maybe not everyone, but with bankers or county people, it feels like they’re looking right at the cracks and spots, how saggy and worn my hands and face are. My wife says I just look like someone who’s worked outside, but I can’t quite believe that.
Do you think your concern about your face and hands is a normal reaction or is it bothering you more than it would bother most people?

I suppose… it’s probably bothering me more than it would most folks. I can’t seem to get past it—how rough my face and hands look, the cracks and spots and all that. Even if my wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, I still feel like bankers or county people are staring at it.
Do you think there's any possibility that your face and hands don't actually look as rough and worn as you think they do?

I guess there’s… some possibility. My wife keeps saying I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors. But I have a hard time believing it, especially around bankers or county people. It feels like they’re looking right at the cracks and spots and sagging.
Do you think your face and hands look rough and worn even when you are alone?
Yeah… even when I’m alone, I still see it. The roughness, the spots, the sagging. It’s harder to shake than I’d like to admit.
Do you think your face and hands would look normal to you if you didn't think about what others might think of them?

I don’t know… maybe a little more normal, if I wasn’t thinking about them staring. But I still can’t really get past how rough my face and hands look—the cracks, spots, the sagging. My wife says it’s just outdoor work showing, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Is there something specific about the cracks, spots, or sagging on your face and hands that bothers you the most?

I guess it’s the overall… worn look. The cracks on my hands and the spots on my face, the sagging some. It just makes me feel like I look rough, and I figure people like bankers or county folks notice it right away. My wife says it’s just from working outdoors, but I can’t quite leave it at that.
Is there one particular crack, spot, or area of sagging that bothers you the most?

Not one single spot, no. It’s more… the whole rough, worn look. My hands with the cracks, my face with the spots and sagging. I just can’t get past it, especially thinking people like bankers or county folks are noticing.
Do you think you would still be concerned about your appearance if the cracks, spots, and sagging on your face and hands were the only things you were worried about?

Yeah… I think so. That’s pretty much what brings me in, honestly. I can’t get past how rough my face and hands look—like the cracks and spots and sagging are what people notice, especially bankers or county folks. My wife says I just look like someone who’s worked outdoors, but… it still bothers me.
Is it the specific appearance of the cracks, spots, and sagging that bothers you, or is it more about not looking a certain way in general?

It’s more the specific look, I guess. My face and hands just look rough and worn to me—the cracks, the spots, the sagging. I get to thinking bankers or county people are staring at all that, even though my wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors.
Is it the idea of not looking perfect or attractive that bothers you, or is it specifically the cracks, spots, and sagging on your face and hands?

It’s specifically the cracks and spots and the sagging, I think. I’m not trying to look perfect exactly… I just can’t get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. Like people at the bank or county office are staring at it, even if my wife says I just look like I’ve worked outdoors.
Is it the thought of being perceived as unattractive in general that bothers you, or is it specifically the appearance of your face and hands?

It’s more my face and hands, yeah. The rough, worn look… the cracks and spots, the sagging. I get stuck thinking those bankers or county people are looking right at it, even though my wife says it’s just from working outdoors.
Is there something about your appearance, other than the cracks, spots, and sagging on your face and hands, that you worry about when you're around bankers or county people?
Not really. I mean… I haven’t noticed anything else in particular. It’s mostly just that rough look on my face and hands.
Do you think you would be satisfied with your appearance if the cracks, spots, and sagging on your face and hands were gone?

I think so… mostly. If the cracks and spots and that sagging weren’t there, I don’t think I’d be sitting there feeling like every banker or county person was looking at me. My wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, but… I can’t get past it.
Is your concern about your appearance mainly about how it affects your social or professional interactions?

Yeah… mostly. It gets in the way of dealing with people. I’ve missed calls with bankers, put off some farm decisions because I couldn’t get myself looking… acceptable enough to sit down with them. And I don’t really agree to photos anymore, even when they’d help with the retreat or craft sales.
Do you think you would be concerned about your overall body image if the issues with your face and hands were resolved?

I don’t think so… not overall, no. It’s really just my face and hands. If they didn’t look so cracked and spotted and worn out, I don’t think I’d be caught up in it like this. It’s when I’m around bankers or county folks that I feel like they’re staring.
